briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and Anthropic Claude 4.5 escalate frontier race as compute bottlenecks tighten

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AGI race has intensified with multiple frontier labs releasing upgraded models amid record funding. Geopolitical tensions around chip exports and model capabilities remain elevated. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability across production systems.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed o4 with advanced reasoning chains while Anthropic released Claude 4.5 Opus. Google DeepMind previewed Gemini 3 and Meta open-sourced Llama 4.1. xAI and DeepSeek continue aggressive scaling. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation gains traction for secure multi-agent coordination.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: New EU AI Act enforcement guidelines target agentic systems. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for automotive, IoT and BCI applications.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA announced Blackwell Ultra shipments ramping to 500k units monthly. Microsoft and Google both broke ground on new 100k GPU clusters in Texas and Arizona. TSMC reports 2nm yield improvements ahead of schedule.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first AGI-level model emerge from a US lab or a Chinese state-backed consortium by 2028?
